content.thinking:
I need to carefully plan out a dwarf rifleman model, around 1.3 meters tall with a stocky Warcraft-style build, before writing anything. I'm working out the coordinate system and proportions—big head, wide shoulders, oversized hands—to define the skeleton structure.

I'm sketching out the hip, spine, neck, head, and jaw joints along with their parent-child relationships and positions, then moving on to figure out the shoulder and arm placement for a readable neutral pose since he'll be holding a blunderbuss.

Deciding the right hand grips the gun at his side with the barrel pointing forward while the left arm stays angled out empty, working out hand and gun coordinates so the stock sits behind the hand and the flared muzzle extends forward.

Now I'm setting up the arm chains with shoulder-elbow-wrist joints for each side, parented to the spine, and giving them a tapering sweep radius for a natural arm shape. For hands I'm keeping it simple with a fist-like sphere at the wrist plus basic finger boxes rather than fully articulated digits.

For legs, I'm defining hip-knee-ankle chains parented to the hips, and considering boot geometry as a box frustum shape covering the lower leg and extending forward for the toe.

I'm adjusting the boot cuff sweep and sole positioning so the foot touches the floor correctly, then setting up the leg radii chain for thigh-knee-ankle before moving on to lofting the torso from the spine bone chain.

For the torso I'm defining lofted cross-section stations along the spine, specifying width/height at each height to shape the barrel chest, but I'm noticing the hips joint and the first spine chain joint may overlap in position, creating a duplicate span I need to resolve.

Simplifying, I'll just use a single spine bone chain rather than separate hips and spine pieces, building a catmull-rom path through three points for spine1 and spine2, parented to hips. Then for the belly, I'm adding a forward bulge by offsetting a loft station slightly in z with its own width and height.

Now I'm settling on the painted color palette: ruddy skin, auburn beard, steel-blue armor with gold trim, brown leather, and deep blue cloth with a plain painted stripe instead of any emblem, avoiding anything that reads as a copied logo.

For gear I'm building up a mottled leather jerkin, oversized spherical pauldrons rimmed with gold torus bands, and a diagonal bandolier draped across the torso using a closed sweep path from shoulder to hip.

I'm defining rough loop points around the chest and back, letting the drape function snap each sample to the nearest torso surface before closing it with a catmull curve. Then I'll sweep a small circular profile along that closed path and bind the weights to the torso bones, possibly adding pouches spaced along the strap.

Now I'm attaching box-shaped pouches and brass shell cylinders along the bandolier path, then working out the belt as a torso loop anchored near the hip joint, reasoning through the correct frame orientation since the hips joint inherits the root's default upward axis.

For the buckle, I'm raycasting against the torso surface to find the front-facing point at the belt height and sticking a gold box there, guarding against a missed hit.

Now I'm working through the legs with cloth trousers, gold-trimmed knee pad spheres, and folded leather boot cuffs with strap buckles. For the head, I'm sizing a dwarf skull as a scaled sphere positioned to keep overall height compact, checking that the neck tucks between the shoulders and the helmet crown stays proportional to the short legs and torso.

I'm placing the head directly on the shoulders Warcraft-style with almost no neck, working out joint positions so the head aims upward with the jaw toward the back. Since local axes get confusing with the head bone aimed up, I'm switching to absolute model-space coordinates for every face feature, starting with the skull sphere, a bulbous reddish nose, and a brow ridge capsule.

Now I'm adding eyes as small white spheres with dark pupils tucked under angled brow rods, pointed ear cones, and a separate lower jaw sphere mostly hidden behind a braided beard that sweeps from the chin down the chest into two braids, parented to the jaw bone.

Shaping the beard sweep with tapering radii and auburn streaked grain coloring...

Now I'm planning beard hair cards: scattering around 120 small pointed tuft shapes along the beard sweep, angled and flowing downward with slight bend and variation, drawn as tinted white/gray SVG strands.

Still writing SVG code...

For braids, I'm thinking of making two plaited chains of spheres or capsules along a path hanging from each side of the beard.

Continuing down the braid path to around hip height, I'll attach both beard and braids to the jaw bone for simplicity, accepting that jaw rotation will carry them along. For the braid segments themselves, I'm alternating sphere shapes with slight scale and tilt variation to create a woven look, using about 16 pieces along the path.

Now I'm adding decorative elements—gold torus rings for hair ties and bobbles at the braid tips—oriented horizontally to wrap around the braid, plus starting on a swooping mustache built from curling capsule paths that sweep outward and down from the nose.

For the mouth, I decide to skip adding teeth or a visible dark slot since the mustache covers it, but add a fun detail: a small clay pipe hanging from the mouth corner, sweeping from the lip out to a bowl shape at the end using a thin wooden-colored curve.

Now I'm designing the helmet as a lathed steel dome sitting above the head, positioning the brim low enough to shade the forehead while keeping the eyes visible underneath, and working out the total height so the figure stays within dwarf proportions. I'm also considering a riveted gold band around the helmet's base, placing small sphere rivets in a ring, and starting to think about a crest ridge running front to back.

I want to add curved bone-colored horns swept from the sides of the helmet up toward the top, tapering in radius, while keeping their peak height reasonable so the silhouette doesn't exceed the dwarf's allowed proportions.

Working through the brim placement, I'm adjusting the lathe profile so the brim extends slightly forward beyond the forehead without clashing the eye and brow positions, checking the head's spherical surface against the brim's front z-coordinate at each y-level to make sure nothing overlaps awkwardly.

For the skin, I'm planning a mottled, ruddy hand-painted look rather than a flat cel shade -- mixing a shadow and light color based on surface normal direction, then layering mottled noise on top for texture, wrapped in a reusable shading helper function.

Still writing paint helper...

Thinking about atlas resolution for each body part — torso, legs, arms, head, beard, helmet, boots — and settling on 2048 paint size for a hand-painted Blizzard-style look without going overboard on texture memory. Now sketching the metal paint pass for steel with scratches.

I'm now planning the blunderbuss geometry: positioning the barrel along a swept path from the right hand, defining a direction vector and origin point at the wrist, then placing the stock behind and barrel front ahead of that origin along the gun's axis.

Working out the barrel sweep with a flaring radius toward the muzzle bell, plus a dark inner disc to fake the hollow bore opening...

Finishing the barrel outline with non-crossing checks, then planning the lathe profile for the brass flared muzzle and steel barrel, plus the full blunderbuss details — flintlock mechanism, trigger guard, ramrod, sling, and a carved wooden stock with gold inlays and dwarf rune etchings.

Now I'm sketching the stock's side profile as a 2D outline to extrude, working out the butt shape, wrist/grip drop below the lock, and forestock taper using coordinate points along the barrel axis.

Plotting the stock outline coordinates...

That segment doesn't cross the others, so the outline holds; I'll use smoothing 0 with a small bevel to avoid any crossing issues, and set the extrusion thickness without taper. For orienting the extrude frame, I need to build a perpendicular "up-ish" vector from the barrel direction, then derive the thickness axis via a cross product, placing the hand grip orientation near u≈-0.09, v≈-0.1.

Now I'm computing the gun anchor position and deriving the hand location from it using the direction vector and perpendicular up vector, working out approximate numeric coordinates for where the hand should sit relative to the gun barrel so the arm's wrist target can be set.

I'm sketching rough shoulder, elbow, and wrist points for the arm, checking segment lengths against the needed shoulder-to-hand distance without worrying about strict inverse kinematics, and deciding to make the hands chunky spheres around radius 0.075.

Now I'm working out the mirrored left arm's relaxed A-pose joints, placing shoulder, elbow, wrist, and the hand sphere position for a fisted hand shape.

I'm sketching the hand geometry: palm sphere dimensions and finger capsules, deciding how the right hand's fingers curl around the grip versus the left hand's loose downward curl.

Working out finger capsule placement and spacing...

Now I'm attaching the blunderbuss gun parts to the right wrist bone using absolute coordinates: a wood stock with painted grain texture, and a swept barrel with steel radii tapering and brass bands marking sections.

For the barrel bands, I'm placing brass torus rings oriented along the barrel axis at a few positions, keeping the barrel octagonal by default section sides. Then I'm adding a lathed brass muzzle bell near the barrel's end with a darker inner cylinder recessed inside it.

For the lock, I'm deciding to place the flintlock mechanism on the outward-facing lateral side of the gun (the side visible to the viewer), starting with a thin box for the lock plate.

Positioning plate with its offset...

Now I'm working out the hammer and frizzen geometry: a curved rod for the cock with a flint jaw, a small brass pan box, and an angled steel frizzen box near the front of the lock plate. For the trigger guard, I'm sketching helper points below the grip to build a curved path for the guard shape.

I notice the fist sphere covering the hand overlaps awkwardly with the trigger guard curve, so I'm repositioning the hand further back along the grip and adjusting the stock outline to accommodate the shift.

I'm checking the arm segment distances look right, with shoulder-to-hand distance around 0.39, then estimating wrist and elbow positions to keep the limb proportions consistent.

Picking an elbow position that gives a reasonable bend between shoulder and wrist, then checking the gun's extents—the butt ends up poking outside the torso's width at the chest, so I'll need to adjust that placement.

Checking clearances near the right pauldron and torso width confirms the arm and gun positioning roughly works, so now I'm moving on to placing the ramrod beneath the barrel, running it from the stock's forend toward the muzzle.

Next I'm working out the sling strap, sagging in a loop from butt to forend with a shallow catenary-like curve and a flat box-section profile for the leather.

Settling on the sling's sag as a quadratic bezier with the control point pulled down, keeping it clear of the leg geometry. Now I'm adding stock details -- a brass buttplate and a decal of gold rune shapes placed sideways on the stock surface, oriented correctly relative to the gun's tilt.

I'm computing the cross product of the extrude's thickness and y-axis vectors to confirm which direction the lateral face points, working through the component math to verify the face normal is along -x, which places the outward face slightly offset in model space on the right side.

For the lock plate, I'll offset its center along x to sit flush against that outward face. I'm also considering decal placement on the stock, checking that the projection direction and position land cleanly on the surface without risking a failed raycast, and deciding to skip adding glow effects to keep things simple.

Actually, I'll add a small gold glow to the gun's rune decal since the texture is transparent where undrawn, so the glow should read nicely as an orange-gold accent without breaking the material requirements. Then I'm moving on to torso extras, starting with steel pauldron spheres scaled and positioned at the shoulder joints.

For the pauldrons I want to tilt them outward with a rotation, add gold rivets and a small spike cone, and layer a second smaller plate on top for that overlapping-plate armor look, all bound to the shoulder joint in the bone chain. Then I'm planning the chest piece: a leather jerkin base with a tabard panel extruded from an outline hanging from waist to knee.

Now I'm working out the tabard's positioning relative to the thighs and belt line, adjusting its hang depth and flare angle so it drapes naturally in front of the body without clipping into the legs.

Reducing the tilt angle to keep the knee outline clear of the leg, and working out the thickness axis via cross product so the belt surface faces forward correctly. Now I'm thinking through the coloring approach—blue cloth with a gold embroidered border defined in surface coordinates.

Writing shader paint logic...

Now I'm thinking about back details -- adding a backpack with bedroll, powder keg, and tin cup to make the dwarf rifleman's rear view more detailed, positioning the leather box pack and cylindrical bedroll along the spine.

I'm also adding a curved powder horn hanging at the left hip via a catmull sweep, with ivory coloring and a brass cap, attached by a strap, while deciding to skip a sheathed sidearm dagger for now.

Now I'm placing belt pouches and a shot bag on the right hip, skipping a pistol addition, and working out knee pad spheres positioned along the leg with rivets instead of gold rims, plus mapping out the chain of hip-knee-ankle joints for the leg sweep geometry.

Adding the toe cap steel sphere and setting leg chain contact points near the ankle. Now I'm working out the neck and head joint hierarchy, parenting the neck to the spine chain's final joint and aiming it upward toward the head position.

Now I'm placing facial features onto the head bone: outward-pointing ear cones, a bulbous nose, cheek spheres, and layered eye spheres with white sclera and blue iris details positioned symmetrically.

I'm also adding a scar detail across the cheek using a thin rotated rod, checking its coordinates against the sphere's surface to make sure it sits flush rather than floating outside the geometry.

I'm considering a chin strap for the helmet but deciding it would clash with the beard, so I'm skipping cheek guards and chin strap, and instead planning a simple nasal guard extending from the helmet's brim.

Actually the nasal guard would collide with the nose geometry, so I'm dropping that too and shifting to horn-shaped helmet horns using a bezier sweep from base to tip with a tapered radius, giving them an ivory color with subtle banding stripes along the y-axis.

Now I'm lathing the helmet itself around the head, defining an outline profile from the crown down through a thin brim, checking that the smoothing level won't cause corner-cutting conflicts given the vertex spacing.

I need to check overall height budget: the helmet plus head should stay under the dwarf's roughly 1.4m target, so I'm nudging the center heights down slightly and deciding whether to skip adding a crest ornament to avoid exceeding that limit.

I'll settle on roughly 1.43m total height. Now I'm adding the gold band and rivets around the helmet, choosing a steel metal palette for the paint, and sketching the beard as a sweeping path of segments from chin down to chest.

For the beard shape, I'm tapering the width and depth along its length so it hugs the torso naturally, checking that it overlaps correctly with the head sphere, jaw, and shoulders without any visible gaps.

Now I'm adding sideburn puffs near the jawline to widen the beard at the sides, then setting up the beard's texture with a grained auburn paint pattern layered over a darker base tone.

Then I'm scattering beard cards across the surface for volume, tinting them with the brighter beard color and shaping their flow downward along the jaw.

For braids, I'm planning two side braids hanging in front of the main beard from chin level down, positioning their path points slightly forward in z so they sit against the beard without clipping into it.

Still refining braid path coordinates...

Checking where the braid and beard overlap near the torso, then adding gold ring ties and a bead at the braid tip. Now I'm sketching the mustache curve points, planning a downward sweep that curls upward at the ends.

I'm plotting a cubic bezier for the mustache shape with tapered radii and pointed caps, noting it sits close to the beard mass but the mouth stays hidden anyway. I'll skip detailed jaw/teeth geometry and move on to the shoulders, adding a gold collar torus around the neck as a finishing touch.

Now I'm sizing the torso shoulders and checking that the broad flat top covers the neck base, then working out a steel gorget collar at the neckline using a torus shape to simplify what would otherwise be a complex lathe profile.

For the chest, I'm figuring out a breastplate loft over the upper torso with stations between y .68 and .92, making the plates slightly larger than the jerkin beneath so they visibly layer on top.

I'm also planning gold trim bands along the plate's edges — sweeping thin gold loops at the bottom (around y .675) and near the top (around y .9) to give that classic steel-and-gold dwarven cuirass look.

Now I want to add a central ridge running up the front of the plate. Figuring out the clock-angle convention is tricky since angle 0 corresponds to the tube's back, so front-facing needs angle 180 — I'll draw a surface line at that angle and run a gold sweep along it to form the ridge.

Working out the cross product confirms the normal faces back, so angle 180 lands at front as the docs suggest — if I'm wrong it just misplaces the ridge harmlessly, and I'm adding gold button accents. I'm keeping an eye on the triangle/part budget, then moving to the backpack: a small leather box positioned behind the chest.

Now I'm routing the shoulder straps as curved tube sweeps from the pack's top corners, over the shoulders, down to the chest, and checking how the rounded end caps' dome radius interacts with the torso's curvature so the strap ends land correctly on the shoulder surface.

Adding narrower shoulder/neck stations tapering the torso loft so it slopes naturally into the neck, then matching a smaller cuirass plate; leaving the hip section flat-capped where the legs attach below.

I'll skip front backpack straps since they'd conflict with the pauldrons, keeping a bandolier instead, and add a bedroll cylinder with simple strap tori secured atop the pack.

I'm adding a hanging cup, a lighter pack flap box, and small gold buckles, then placing brass shell cylinders along the bandolier path -- though they're lying flat along the strap direction rather than perpendicular, which isn't quite right but I'll leave it as pouches for now.

Mapping out the bandolier's draped path across the chest, plotting a loop of points from right shoulder down to left hip and around the back to keep the strap shape believable in 3D space.

I'm deciding that the strap should drape against both torso and cuirass surfaces combined, choosing a small lift and tube radius so it sits visibly above the plate without looking detached, and checking the belt placement doesn't conflict with where the bandolier crosses near the hip.

Now I'm shifting to setting up imports carefully, planning to pull in the frame, path, and paint utilities while avoiding unused names that would break typechecking, and using THREE.Vector3 directly for vector math instead of a custom type.

Setting up gun geometry vectors...

Still writing arm chain logic...

Defining color palette constants...

Still writing paint helper...

Gloves get dark leather with a gold cuff accent, and I'm adding subtle woven grain texture to the cloth paint. Now I'm starting the actual build function, setting up the builder and skeleton with the hips joint as the root.

Building spine and neck joints...

Comparing against the jerkin's interpolated widths, I'm nudging the plate armor stations slightly larger to account for added bulk, adjusting width and height values at each station height.

I'm checking that waist tunic shows through between the jerkin's end and the plate's start, with a belt visible, and verifying that the gold trim loops align near the bottom flat cap.

Adding the trim sweep and surface loop logic...

Setting up the belt loop on the torso surface next.

Working out the belt buckle: raycasting against the torso to find the attachment point, then sticking a small gold box there embedded partway into the surface, with the box's thin dimension aligned along the surface normal for correct orientation.

Now I'm positioning pouches around the belt -- placing boxes at left and right hip offsets and one at the back, approximating coordinates based on the torso's width and estimating rotation angles so they sit flush against the curved surface.

For the powder horn, I'm thinking through hanging it from the left hip with a curved path built from a few control points, giving it a tapered radius with an ivory body and a brass cap cylinder at the base, positioned to clear the hanging arm. Now I'm moving on to building the legs with a loop over left and right sides...

Writing leg chain code...

Still building boot geometry...

Positioning the gold strap and buckle accents, then adding knee pad geometry with steel spheres and gold rim studs...

Now I'm working out pauldron placement and rotation, calculating how the shoulder armor should droop outward based on left/right side mirroring.

Placing the gold spike on top of the pauldron, sized to stay below the helmet, then considering a decorative torus band around the pauldron rim instead of individual rivets.

I'm figuring out that rotating the torus with Euler order XYZ applies the z-rotation first, which has no effect on a shape symmetric about its own z-axis, so I need to reorder the tilt so it actually lays the ring flat.

Writing geometry helper...

I'm renaming it "hoop" to avoid clashing with the body's ring method, then sizing the pauldron band around the shoulder sphere with a slight scale asymmetry so it sits right at the equator without clipping into the arm sweep below.

Now I'm placing a steel gorget hoop at the neck junction, then moving into the head bones -- building the skull as a scaled sphere attached to the head bone, with the nose as a small sphere positioned just below the brow, while checking that painted normals still behave correctly on the non-uniformly scaled geometry.

I'm sketching the jaw as another scaled sphere overlapping the skull for a chin effect, deciding to skip visible teeth since the mustache will hide them, and now working out brow ridges as capsule rods anchored to the head bone, lining up the helmet brim radius so it clears the forward-projecting face.

Next I'm figuring out the beard geometry as a swept shape attached to the jaw bone, deciding on round start and end caps so it blends smoothly into the head and tapers to a soft point, and working out the radius function that controls how the beard narrows along its length.

I'm checking whether the beard's rounded start cap might extend too far upward and overlap the jaw or head sphere, since the dome at the path's start could bulge backward beyond the intended beard region near the eyes and nose.

The beard dome barely pokes past the skull front at y 1.1, but since that's the mouth/chin zone it just reads as the beard bursting from the lower face — moving the start to y 1.09 cleans it up. I'll go with a wide shovel beard made of ~120 scattered cards, keep the mustache, and include the pipe since it's cheap. Final concept: dwarf rifleman with braided beard, now thinking about the backpack.

For the gun, I'm computing bone attachment points off the right arm, and figuring out the rune decal orientation on the stock — since the viewer at -x facing +x has their right pointing toward +z (the barrel direction), the runes should read correctly along that axis.

Now I'm drafting an SVG of angular gold rune glyphs, strokes in a warm amber tone, laid out as distinct symbol shapes across the viewBox.

With that done, I'm thinking through how to apply glow effects to the decal mesh and whether additional surface details—embroidery, beard tufts, ornamental accents—are worth adding, deciding most can be handled through paint loops rather than extra decals.

Now I'm working out the bandolier strap using a drape sweep along a closed catmull path, figuring out how to express the box cross-section as a radius function returning sideways and normal half-extents.

Since the orientation along the path is uncertain and could render edge-on, I'll switch to a simple round strap with a small circle radius instead, then plan to attach pouches along that path using an `along` helper that places stick geometry at even intervals, embedding them slightly into the strap surface.

I'm figuring out that pouches should only appear on the front portion of the loop, restricting the parameter range to roughly t=0.05–0.42 with about 7 items, and sizing each pouch box to sit centered on the strap with its long axis following the path tangent.

For variety I'll alternate between pouches and bullet cartridges by index, using rotated cylinder geometry so the cartridges lie crosswise across the strap like brass rounds. Now I'm moving on to adding card details into the beard tuft geometry.

Adding scatter options...

Now I'm checking the stick geometry types for frame inputs, then adding backpack extras and figuring out how the right hand grips the stock, wrapping fingers around it relative to the hand center and lateral thickness.

Still placing hand geometry...

Then I'll add a gold wrist ring oriented along the forearm direction for both arms, followed by steel vambraces. Now I'm sketching the armBuild function that creates the shoulder-elbow-wrist chain and sweeps the limb geometry along it.

Still writing arm geometry...

Checking wrist-to-hand distances and arm curves for both sides look fine. Now setting up the gun parts attached to the right wrist bone, starting with the stock geometry.

Still writing stock extrude code...

Writing wood shading logic...

For the barrel, I'm sweeping a polyline path with varying radii to taper the shape, using flat caps near the breech where the stock covers it, starting the breech section around u=-0.08 with brass tang details and running the barrel to u=0.5. I'm making it octagonal and faceted with 8 crisp sides rather than smooth, and planning brass hoop bands at several points along its length.

Now I'm lathing the bell shape at the muzzle end with a faceted outline and brass coloring, adding a darker inner cylinder to suggest depth into the bore, and placing brass rings near the bell mouth. I'm also positioning the lock plate on the side of the stock near the breech.

Checking proportions, I realize the hand/grip position overlaps slightly with the lock plate, so I'm nudging the hand lower and the grip drop point to avoid the collision.

Now I'm placing the cock and hammer mechanism: a steel rod running from the lock plate base up to the jaws, gold jaws at the top, and a small brass pan box positioned forward of the lock, oriented along the gun's direction axis with lateral, normal, and length dimensions sized appropriately.

Still laying out hardware...

Next I'm positioning the frizzen as a steel rod with a small gold flint piece, then adding a trigger guard shaped via a curved path and a brass trigger rod, before setting up the ramrod as a long thin rod running nearly the full length of the barrel.

Now I'm adding brass thimbles as small cylinders to hold the ramrod along the stock, considering a forend cap, and working out the buttplate geometry as a brass box sized and oriented against the butt end of the stock.

I'm also adding gold rivets as tiny spheres scattered along the grip area, and considering whether to skip detailing like front sights or a powder flask for now.

Switching to the part-building helper, I'll write it so each piece is placed with a bone, position, and color parameter, then call it repeatedly for each component.

Now I'm positioning body parts relative to spine joints, like chest and hips, and defining the belt and tabard geometry with extrusion offsets anchored near the hip height.

Checking vertical placement so the tabard sits flush under the belt and clears the thighs without gaps, working through z-depth at different torso heights to make sure it stays tight against the body front but still covers the thigh gap.

For the back, I'm adding a similar leather flap behind the torso with its own orientation vectors and outline, making sure its depth doesn't poke through the torso loft at the waist.

Now I'm defining a braid helper function that builds a curved path using Catmull-Rom control points for the hair strand.

Still placing braid details...

I'm adding the pipe bowl shape with a cone cylinder, then a small glowing ember disc at the top in warm orange, plus a rune glow detail. Now I'm double-checking my import list has everything I need—THREE, builder helpers, curves, color utilities, and glow—and planning to use stripes texture for the horns.

Checking type signatures and overload compatibility for the various builder methods—sweep, rod, spike, part, lathe—to make sure the tuple and array arguments I'm passing match what they expect.

Still mapping out variable usage...

Now I'm building the bedroll geometry on the chest and the strap hoops, plus starting the backpack's main box dimensions.

Still working out backpack placement...

Now sketching the helmet crest profile with a curved outline tapering from the brow toward the top, defining the points for the extrusion shape.

Adjusting crest color to gold with thin bevel, keeping total height around 1.42. I'm working out the horn geometry, positioning its base and tip against the helmet's radius profile, plus placing the face scar, eyes, and double-checking the head sphere sits properly inside the helmet front.

Checking the skull radius against the helmet brim near the forehead to confirm clearance, then moving on to write the part definitions with proper direction and axis settings, including optional sleeve caps for the arms.

Now I'm positioning the gloves and hands, placing the palm as a scaled sphere and building out finger capsules for each hand with offsets for base and tip positions, plus a separate thumb placement.
